report.source_text: The patient underwent a standard three-port 25-gauge pars plana vitrectomy in the left eye first. After core vitrectomy, intravitreal triamcinolone acetonide was injected to stain posterior cortical vitreous and induce posterior vitreous detachment. Air–fluid exchange was done, and ILM was stained with brilliant blue green. ILM peeling was carried out about 2-disc diameters around the macular hole. A non-expansile mixture of 14% C3F8 Gas tamponade was given. The patient was asked to maintain a face-down position for 10 hours a day for 7 days. To minimise the risks associated with bilateral simultaneous surgery, the surgery for the right eye was performed 4 weeks later.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Bilateral idiopathic macular hole in a young female
clinician.trajectory_summary: A woman in her early 30s presented with progressive bilateral central vision loss and metamorphopsia over 6 months. Examination revealed reduced visual acuity bilaterally, normal anterior segments (clear crystalline lens, no inflammation), and fundoscopic findings of full-thickness macular holes confirmed by spectral domain OCT. Axial length measurements (24.02 mm OD, 24.15 mm OS) excluded high myopia. The patient underwent sequential 25-gauge pars plana vitrectomy with ILM peeling (left eye first, right eye 4 weeks later) using perfluoropropane gas tamponade. At 10 weeks postoperatively, both macular holes achieved anatomical closure (type 2A OD, type 1B OS) with best-corrected visual acuity improving to 6/9p in the right eye and 6/9 in the left eye.
